findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a pan of raw fish observed to be above a box of avocados in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The pan of raw fish was moved to be below the avocados. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order and that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler shelves were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. Discussed cleaning the shelves with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There is observed to be a large pot of rice cooling that is set on a trash can and there is a sheet pan that is being used to prepare salmon that is set on top of another trash can. This was discussed with the PIC. Trash cans should not be used as counters, as they are not clean, sanitized food-contact surfaces. Cease using trash cans as counters and either obtain more preparation tables or use other surfaces in the facility, such as the top of the chest freezer.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of breaded raw eel and a container of raw shrimp that were observed to be above a container of cut ginger in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The ginger was moved over to avoid being under the raw eel and raw shrimp. The PIC was educated on proper storage order and appeared to be educated on it. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
There are three employees other than the PIC, who is a Certified Food Protection Manager, that are observed to not have a food handler certificate. This was discussed with the PIC who was educated that all employees who are handling food need to have their food handler certificate. Ensure that all food handling employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.
